source: Structure derived from the uploaded HelloInterview 'System Design in a Hurry' Introduction chapter (Interviewer Rubric, interview types, prep guidance, common questions). The Introduction is the only chapter present in the PDF; Core Concepts / Key Technologies / Delivery Framework bodies were not included, so the delivery framework below is a standard, widely-taught skeleton seeded for expansion and the topic bodies are placeholders to be filled from the full guide. No PDF content was fabricated.

delivery_framework.title: Delivery Framework
delivery_framework.note: A repeatable track to run on during the interview. Standard skeleton (full step bodies are in the complete guide, not in the uploaded Introduction).

steps.name: Requirements
steps.detail: Clarify functional requirements (what the system does) and non-functional requirements (scale, latency, availability, consistency). Establish scope and what is explicitly out of scope.

steps.name: Core Entities & API
steps.detail: Identify the core entities/data the system manages, then define the API (endpoints or RPCs) the client uses to interact with them.

steps.name: High-Level Design
steps.detail: Draw the main components (clients, services, datastores, queues) and the data flow that satisfies the functional requirements end to end.

steps.name: Deep Dives
steps.detail: Revisit the non-functional requirements and harden the design: scaling bottlenecks, caching, sharding/partitioning, replication, consistency, and failure modes.

interview_types.name: Product Design
interview_types.detail: Design the system behind a product (e.g. a ride-sharing app). Primary focus of the guide.

interview_types.name: Infrastructure Design
interview_types.detail: Design an infrastructure use case, e.g. a rate limiter or message queue. Primary focus of the guide.

interview_types.name: Object-Oriented / Low-Level Design
interview_types.detail: Design the class structure of a system. Covered by a separate 'Low-Level Design in a Hurry' guide.

interview_types.name: Applied ML System Design
interview_types.detail: Design an ML-backed system. Covered by a separate 'ML System Design in a Hurry' guide.

interview_types.name: ML Infrastructure Design
interview_types.detail: Design the infrastructure that trains/serves ML models.

rubric.detail: Decompose an under-specified problem, prioritize, and navigate to a solution. Often the most important dimension.
failures: Failing to deliver a working system

rubric.detail: Solve each piece and integrate them into a cohesive whole. Relies on Core Concepts.
Apply best practices and current technology correctly. Relies on Key Technologies.
Explain complex ideas clearly, take feedback, and collaborate.

topics.title: Core Concepts
topics.summary: Foundational building blocks: scaling, CAP theorem, consistency models, availability, and partitioning. (Bodies to be populated from the full guide.)

topics.title: Key Technologies
topics.summary: Common building blocks referenced in the guide (e.g. Redis for caching, Elasticsearch + inverted indexes for search). (Bodies to be populated from the full guide.)

topics.title: Patterns
topics.summary: Recurring design patterns for common sub-problems. (Bodies to be populated from the full guide.)

questions.title: Design a Ride-Sharing Service (like Uber)
questions.prompt: Design the backend for a ride-sharing service. Support riders requesting rides, matching to nearby drivers, real-time location tracking, and trip lifecycle.

questions.title: Design a Rate Limiter
questions.prompt: Design a rate limiter that restricts how many requests a client may make in a time window.
considerations: Token bucket vs sliding window vs fixed window

questions.title: Design Instagram / a Photo Feed
questions.prompt: Design a photo-sharing service with a home feed of posts from followed users.

questions.title: Design Yelp / Nearby Business Search
questions.prompt: Design a service to find and review businesses near a location.

questions.title: Design Google Docs / Collaborative Editing
questions.prompt: Design a collaborative real-time document editor.

prep_guidance.time: If brand new to system design, dedicate focused time or spread study over 3-4 weeks; less if already experienced.
prep_guidance.how_to_use: Read in order and skip what you already know. Practice with worked solutions to common problems, then attempt real practice problems and quizzes.
